bounded_statement: The selected result (Welch two-sample t-test on 48 TDS readings, 24 per grind group, t = 8.456, df = 45.1, p < 0.0001) enters each declared independent unit (vessel_id) into a row-independent two-sample t-test four times: the design has only 12 independent vessels (6 coarse, 6 fine), each sampled at four draw times, but every row was supplied to stats.ttest_ind as a separate independent observation. The four within-vessel readings are strongly correlated (TDS rises monotonically within every vessel), so the reported per-group n of 24 and df of 45.1 overstate the information content of the data and the p-value and standard errors of the selected result are anti-conservative relative to a vessel-level analysis with 6 units per group.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the repeated-sampling design and the fact that every row was used as one observation, so the pooling is not concealed; moreover, per-vessel mean TDS values computed from the CSV separate the groups completely (coarse vessel means ~1.08 to 1.22 %, fine vessel means ~1.32 to 1.47 %, no overlap), so a correct vessel-level analysis with 6 units per group would likely still find a significant fine-versus-coarse difference in the same direction. This mitigates the practical consequence for the direction of the conclusion, but does not change the fact that the selected result's n, df, t and p were computed by entering each vessel four times into a procedure that assumes independent rows.

source_refs.quoted_text:
48 total-dissolved-solids (TDS) readings taken from laboratory cold-brew
steeping vessels. Each vessel was loaded with a single grind setting and
sampled at draw times of 6, 12, 18 and 24 hours.

evidence.description: The data description declares vessel_id as the independent unit and states each vessel appears in four rows (one per draw time), with grind constant within a vessel — so rows are repeated measurements of the same unit, not independent observations.
evidence.observed_value: 12 vessels x 4 draws = 48 rows; independent unit = vessel_id

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one aliquot drawn from one steeping vessel at one draw time
Independent unit column: vessel_id

- vessel_id: label of the steeping vessel, V01 through V12. Each vessel appears
  in four rows, one per draw time.

- grind: the grind setting loaded into that vessel, "coarse" or "fine". The
  setting is a property of the vessel, so it is the same in all four of a
  vessel's rows.

evidence.description: The workflow pools all row-level TDS values by grind setting without any reference to vessel_id and feeds them to a two-sample t-test that treats each row as an independent observation; vessel_id is never used anywhere in analysis.py.
evidence.observed_value: stats.ttest_ind(fine, coarse, equal_var=False) applied to 24 row-level values per group from 6 vessels per group

evidence.observed_value: n = 48 rows (24 fine, 24 coarse), df = 45.1, p < 0.0001 versus 12 independent vessels

source_refs.quoted_text:
Welch two-sample t-test (two-sided, unequal variances) comparing the TDS
readings recorded at the fine grind setting with those recorded at the
coarse setting. Every row of the data file was supplied to the test as one
observation.
[selected-result] Welch two-sample t-test on 48 TDS readings (24 fine, 24 coarse): mean difference fine minus coarse = 0.2521 percentage points, t = 8.456, df = 45.1, p < 0.0001.

evidence.description: Within-vessel readings are strongly positively correlated, not independent: TDS increases monotonically with steep time within every vessel (e.g., V01 rises 1.06 -> 1.13 -> 1.23 -> 1.26), so the four rows per vessel carry far less than four independent observations' worth of information about the grind effect.
evidence.observed_value: V01 tds_percent across draws: 1.06, 1.13, 1.23, 1.26 (monotone increasing; same pattern in all 12 vessels)

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the finding in three ways. (1) Could the 48 rows legitimately be independent observations? No: the data description explicitly names vessel_id as the independent-unit column and states each vessel is sampled four times with grind fixed per vessel, and the CSV shows monotone within-vessel TDS trajectories confirming strong within-unit correlation. (2) Does the workflow aggregate to one value per vessel or otherwise model the repeated draws (e.g., vessel means, mixed model, clustered errors) anywhere? No: the string vessel_id appears nowhere in analysis.py; tds_for() filters rows only by grind and the pooled row-level arrays go straight into stats.ttest_ind. (3) Do the reported statistics correspond to a unit-level analysis by coincidence? No: the report states n = 24 per group and df = 45.1, which are only obtainable by treating all 48 rows as independent; a vessel-level Welch test would have n = 6 per group and at most 10 df. All three attempts failed to overturn the finding, so the issue is demonstrated. The only mitigating observation is that vessel-level means still separate the groups, so the direction of the conclusion is likely robust even though the selected result's inferential statistics are inflated.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py never references the independent-unit column vessel_id: tds_for() pools tds_percent from all rows matching a grind setting, and main() passes these pooled row-level arrays directly to stats.ttest_ind (a procedure that assumes each supplied value is an independent observation), with no per-vessel aggregation or model term accounting for repeated draws from the same vessel.
